instructions.name: ame.acquire
instructions.description: Requests the entire AME backend; see <<ame-backend-management-operators>>.

instructions.name: ame.release
instructions.description: Releases the entire AME backend; see <<ame-backend-management-operators>>.
instructions.operation: release the backend held by this hart

instructions.name: agettyp
instructions.description:
Gets the 32-bit datatype descriptor of an `Acc` register by reading from `Ad`
and zero-extending it to XLEN in `X[rd]`.

instructions.name: asettyp
instructions.description:
Sets the datatype of an `Acc` register and clears every physical storage bit of
the accumulator to zero.  This is a raw-bit clear, not conversion to the new
datatype's semantic zero.  The new 32-bit descriptor is `X[rs1][31:0]`; any
upper X-register bits are ignored.

instructions.name: mabs.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise absolute value of the tensor in `ms1`, stored into `md`.
For a standard floating-point operand, either zero produces `+0`, either
infinity produces `+infinity`, and every representable finite result is exact.

instructions.name: mabsdiff.ew
instructions.description: Elementwise absolute difference of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.

instructions.name: mabsdiff.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise absolute difference between a scalar constant from integer
register `rs1` and every element of square `ms2`, and stores the result in `md`.

instructions.name: madd.ew
instructions.description: Elementwise addition of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.

instructions.name: madd.ew.x
instructions.description:
Adds a scalar constant from integer register `rs1` to every element of square `ms2`
and stores the result in `md`.

instructions.name: mand.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise bitwise AND of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.
For standard datatypes, `Md[ms1]`, `Md[ms2]`, and `Md[md]` shall be the same
integer datatype, and the operation applies to the raw element bits.  An
accepted custom tuple shall define its operand widths, raw-bit operation, and
destination representation.

instructions.name: mand.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise bitwise AND of a scalar constant from integer register `rs1`
with every element of square `ms2` and stores the result in `md`.
For standard datatypes, `Md[ms2]` and `Md[md]` shall be the same integer
datatype, and the converted scalar and matrix elements are operated on as raw
bits.  An accepted custom tuple shall define its operand widths, raw-bit
operation, and destination representation.

instructions.name: mandnot.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise bitwise AND of `ms1` with the bitwise complement of `ms2`, stored into `md`.
For standard datatypes, `Md[ms1]`, `Md[ms2]`, and `Md[md]` shall be the same
integer datatype, and the operation applies to the raw element bits.  An
accepted custom tuple shall define its operand widths, raw-bit operation, and
destination representation.

instructions.name: mandnot.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise bitwise AND of a scalar constant from integer register `rs1`
with the bitwise complement of every element of square `ms2` and stores the result in
`md`.
For standard datatypes, `Md[ms2]` and `Md[md]` shall be the same integer
datatype, and the converted scalar and matrix elements are operated on as raw
bits.  An accepted custom tuple shall define its operand widths, raw-bit
operation, and destination representation.

instructions.name: mcmovge.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise two-way conditional move using the numeric comparison of each
`ms1` element with zero as the predicate.
If the `ms1` element is greater than or equal to zero, the corresponding `ms2`
element is written to `md`; otherwise the pre-instruction `md` element is
preserved bit-for-bit.
The predicate datatype `Md[ms1]` shall define the ordered comparison used by
the `Operation`, and `Md[ms2]` and `Md[md]` shall be identical.  A tuple that
violates either requirement is unsupported under
<<norm:ame_op_supported_contract,the unsupported-datatype-tuple contract>>.
An accepted custom tuple shall define the selected-value representation.

instructions.name: mcmovlt.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise two-way conditional move using the numeric comparison of each
`ms1` element with zero as the predicate.
If the `ms1` element is less than zero, the corresponding `ms2` element is
written to `md`; otherwise the pre-instruction `md` element is preserved
bit-for-bit.
The predicate datatype `Md[ms1]` shall define the ordered comparison used by
the `Operation`, and `Md[ms2]` and `Md[md]` shall be identical.  A tuple that
violates either requirement is unsupported under
<<norm:ame_op_supported_contract,the unsupported-datatype-tuple contract>>.
An accepted custom tuple shall define the selected-value representation.

instructions.name: mcmpge.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise greater-or-equal comparison of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.
For standard datatypes, the sources are integer or floating-point and the
destination is integer.  The comparison is ordered: a NaN operand makes it
false, and `-0` compares equal to `+0`.  A true result is represented by all
one bits and a false result by all zero bits in the destination element.  An
accepted custom tuple shall define its ordering and these result bit patterns.

instructions.name: mcmpge.ew.x
instructions.description:
Compares a scalar constant from integer register `rs1` against every element of square
`ms2`, storing -1 (all bits set) where the scalar is greater than or equal to the element,
and 0 otherwise, into `md`.
For standard datatypes, the compared values are integer or floating-point and
the destination is integer.  The comparison is ordered: a NaN operand makes it
false, and `-0` compares equal to `+0`.  A true result is represented by all
one bits and a false result by all zero bits in the destination element.  An
accepted custom tuple shall define its ordering and these result bit patterns.

instructions.name: mcmplt.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise less-than comparison of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.
For standard datatypes, the sources are integer or floating-point and the
destination is integer.  The comparison is ordered: a NaN operand makes it
false, and `-0` compares equal to `+0`.  A true result is represented by all
one bits and a false result by all zero bits in the destination element.  An
accepted custom tuple shall define its ordering and these result bit patterns.

instructions.name: mcmplt.ew.x
instructions.description:
Compares a scalar constant from integer register `rs1` against every element of square
`ms2`, storing -1 (all bits set) where the scalar is strictly less than the element,
and 0 otherwise, into `md`.
For standard datatypes, the compared values are integer or floating-point and
the destination is integer.  The comparison is ordered: a NaN operand makes it
false, and `-0` compares equal to `+0`.  A true result is represented by all
one bits and a false result by all zero bits in the destination element.  An
accepted custom tuple shall define its ordering and these result bit patterns.

instructions.name: mcolbcast.ew.x
instructions.synopsis: Broadcast one column to all columns
instructions.description:
Broadcasts column `c` (from integer register `rs1`) of `ms2` to every column of
`md`, independently for every row.
If `c` is outside `[0, sqrt(AME_NELEM))`, an `Illegal Instruction` exception is raised.
The `rs1` operand is a fixed-type control scalar: its low 32 bits are interpreted as an
unsigned integer column index.  It does not read `CSR[amestype]` and does not undergo
AME datatype conversion.
`md` and `ms2` each contain exactly one logical square.  Packed datatypes are
unsupported and are handled according to
<<norm:ame_op_supported_contract,the unsupported-datatype-tuple contract>>.
`Md[ms2]` and `Md[md]` shall be identical; a mismatch is an unsupported
datatype tuple.

instructions.name: mcolgather.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise column gather: for each element in each row, uses the corresponding index from `ms2`
to select a column from the same row of `ms1`, and stores the result into `md`.
`md`, `ms1`, and `ms2` each contain exactly one logical square.  Packed
datatypes are unsupported.  `Md[ms1]` and `Md[md]` shall be identical, and
`Md[ms2]` shall be an integer datatype.  A tuple that violates any of these
requirements is handled according to
<<norm:ame_op_supported_contract,the unsupported-datatype-tuple contract>>.
The low 32 raw bits of each `ms2` index element form an unsigned U32 value;
higher element bits are ignored, and an element narrower than 32 bits is
zero-extended.  The effective column index is the low
`log2(sqrt(AME_NELEM))` bits of that U32 value.  Higher U32 bits are ignored,
so an index element never raises an exception regardless of its value.
instructions.operation:
idx[i,j] = the effective column index of B[i,j] defined above
D[i,j] = A[i, idx[i,j]]

instructions.name: mcolid.ew
instructions.synopsis: Write zero-based column index to every element
instructions.description:
Writes to each element of the M register group `md` the zero-based index of
the column containing that element.  With `N = sqrt(AME_NELEM)`, every
element of column `j` receives the value `j`, for `0 <= j < N`.
The index value is represented in the destination datatype `Md[md]`.  The
destination datatype must be a supported *integer* datatype in which the
largest index `N-1` is exactly representable; otherwise `amestatus.UN` is
set and no register is written.

instructions.name: mcolshift.ew.x
instructions.synopsis: Elementwise column shift by scalar offset
instructions.description:
Performs an elementwise column shift of `ms2` by offset `c` and stores the result
in `md`.  The offset is obtained by interpreting the low 32 bits of integer
register `rs1` as a signed two's-complement integer.  This fixed-type control
scalar does not read `CSR[amestype]`.
Elements shifted beyond the column boundary are filled with zero (no wrap-around).
`md` and `ms2` each contain exactly one logical square.  Packed datatypes are
unsupported and are handled according to
<<norm:ame_op_supported_contract,the unsupported-datatype-tuple contract>>.
`Md[ms2]` and `Md[md]` shall be identical; a mismatch is an unsupported
datatype tuple.

instructions.name: mcolunzip.ew
instructions.synopsis: Column unzip (de-interleave columns from two inputs)
instructions.description:
De-interleaves the columns of the two-square logical source formed by the
logical source square at `ms1` followed by the logical source square at
`ms2`, and writes the two result squares back into `ms1` and `ms2`.  Each
operand is both a source and a destination.
Let `N = sqrt(AME_NELEM)`; `i` ranges over rows and `j` is in `[0, N/2)`.
`A` and `B` are the pre-instruction logical squares at `ms1` and
`ms2`.  Even-indexed columns of the logical source are collected into
`ms1`; odd-indexed columns into `ms2`.  Each of `ms1` and `ms2` contains exactly
one logical square.
`ms1` and `ms2` must name distinct M registers; an equal pair raises an
`Illegal Instruction` exception before any register is read or written.
The datatypes of `ms1` and `ms2` must match; if they differ, `amestatus.UN`
is set and no register is written.
After the instruction-specific source selection and result placement, every
element is copied bit-for-bit in that common datatype representation.  This
preserves floating-point NaN payloads and signed zeros, and all custom-datatype
representations.
Packed datatypes are unsupported and are handled according to
<<norm:ame_op_supported_contract,the unsupported-datatype-tuple contract>>.
Inverse of `mcolzip.ew`.

instructions.name: mcolzip.ew
instructions.synopsis: Column zip (interleave columns from two inputs)
instructions.description:
Interleaves columns from the logical source square at `ms1` and the logical
source square at `ms2`, and writes the two result squares back into `ms1`
and `ms2`.  Each operand is both a source and a destination.
Let `N = sqrt(AME_NELEM)`; `i` ranges over rows and `j` is in `[0, N/2)`.
`A` and `B` are the pre-instruction logical squares at `ms1` and
`ms2`.  Columns from `A` appear at even positions and columns from `B`
appear at odd positions within the two-square logical result.  Each
of `ms1` and `ms2` contains exactly one logical square.
`ms1` and `ms2` must name distinct M registers; an equal pair raises an
`Illegal Instruction` exception before any register is read or written.
The datatypes of `ms1` and `ms2` must match; if they differ, `amestatus.UN`
is set and no register is written.
After the instruction-specific source selection and result placement, every
element is copied bit-for-bit in that common datatype representation.  This
preserves floating-point NaN payloads and signed zeros, and all custom-datatype
representations.
Packed datatypes are unsupported and are handled according to
<<norm:ame_op_supported_contract,the unsupported-datatype-tuple contract>>.
Inverse of `mcolunzip.ew`.

instructions.name: mconv.ew
instructions.synopsis: Convert element data between supported datatypes, including packed and non-packed representations
instructions.description:
Converts element data between supported datatypes.
The source datatype is determined from `Md[ms1]` and the destination datatype from `Md[md]`.
The source and destination datatypes may each be a packed or a non-packed datatype; no
particular packedness combination is required.  Both operands are formed by the common
operand-formation rules, so the instruction's square count is `N_sq = max(pack_factor)`
and every operand spans exactly `N_sq` squares.
`mconv.ew` converts each element of the formed logical source operand from the source
datatype to the destination datatype and writes the result squares to the formed logical
destination operand.  A packed source with a non-packed destination therefore expands
the source squares; a non-packed source with a packed destination compresses them; and
operands with the same packedness convert each element without changing the square layout.
Element conversion follows the common datatype conversion rules; unsupported conversion tuples set
`amestatus.UN` and do not modify any register.
instructions.operation: D = convert(A) over every element of the formed logical operands

instructions.name: mbcast.m.x
instructions.synopsis: Convert an X-register scalar and broadcast it to an M operand
instructions.description:
Interprets the low 32 bits of `X[rs2]` as an AME datatype encoding and the
X-register bit pattern as one scalar of that datatype, where
`src_dtype = X[rs2][31:0]`.  If `sizeof(src_dtype)` is less than XLEN, only
the low `sizeof(src_dtype)` bits are used and higher X-register bits are
ignored; if it is greater than XLEN, `X[rs1]` is zero-extended to that width.
The scalar is converted once to the destination datatype `Md[md]` as defined
by the accepted exact operation/datatype tuple, then written to every logical
element of `M[md]`.  Packed destinations receive the value in every logical
packed element.
The source and destination datatype encodings must be supported, and the
source-to-destination conversion must be supported.  Otherwise,
`amestatus.UN` is set and no destination state is modified.  The instruction
does not read `CSR[amestype]`; the source datatype is supplied
explicitly by `X[rs2]`.
instructions.operation: D[i] = convert(X[rs1], source datatype X[rs2], destination datatype Md[md])

instructions.name: mcos.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise cosine of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
For a standard floating-point operand, an infinite input is invalid and
`cos(±0)` is `+1`.  The result is an implementation-defined approximation; the
implementation shall document the maximum error in ulp for each supported
operation/datatype tuple.

instructions.name: mexp2.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise base-2 exponentiation of the tensor in `ms1`, stored into `md`.
For a standard floating-point operand, `exp2(+infinity)` is `+infinity`,
`exp2(-infinity)` is `+0`, and `exp2(±0)` is `+1`.  The result is an
implementation-defined approximation; the implementation shall document the
maximum error in ulp for each supported operation/datatype tuple.

instructions.name: mfrintm.ew
instructions.description:
Rounds each floating-point element of `ms1` to an integral value toward minus
infinity (floor) and stores the result in `md`.
For a standard floating-point operand, infinity is unchanged, zero preserves its
sign, and a representable integral result is exact.  This instruction-specific
rounding direction overrides the destination datatype rounding-mode field.

instructions.name: mfrintn.ew
instructions.synopsis: Round float to integral (nearest, ties to even)
instructions.description:
Rounds each floating-point element of `ms1` to the nearest integral value, with
ties rounded to even, and stores the result in `md`.
For a standard floating-point operand, infinity is unchanged, zero preserves its
sign, and a representable integral result is exact.  This instruction-specific
rounding direction overrides the destination datatype rounding-mode field.

instructions.name: mfrintp.ew
instructions.description:
Rounds each floating-point element of `ms1` to an integral value toward positive
infinity (ceil) and stores the result in `md`.
For a standard floating-point operand, infinity is unchanged, zero preserves its
sign, and a representable integral result is exact.  This instruction-specific
rounding direction overrides the destination datatype rounding-mode field.

instructions.name: mfrintz.ew
instructions.description:
Rounds each floating-point element of `ms1` to an integral value toward zero
(truncate) and stores the result in `md`.
For a standard floating-point operand, infinity is unchanged, zero preserves its
sign, and a representable integral result is exact.  This instruction-specific
rounding direction overrides the destination datatype rounding-mode field.

instructions.name: mgettyp
instructions.description:
Gets the 32-bit datatype descriptor of an `M` register by reading from `Md`
and zero-extending it to XLEN in `X[rd]`.

instructions.name: mhdiff.ew
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise half-difference using each `ms2` element as the
minuend and the corresponding `ms1` element as the subtrahend, and stores the
result in `md`.

instructions.name: mhdiff.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise half-difference using each `ms2` element as the
minuend and the scalar from `rs1` as the subtrahend, and stores the result in
`md`.

instructions.name: mldexp.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise scale of `ms1` by a power of two given by `ms2`, stored into `md`.
For a standard tuple, `Md[ms2]` shall be an integer datatype.  An accepted
custom tuple shall define `ms2` elements as integral exponents.
For standard floating-point data operands, a signed zero or signed infinity
preserves its sign.  The exact scaled result is rounded once on conversion to
the destination datatype.

instructions.name: mldexp.ew.x
instructions.description:
Scales every element of square `ms2` by a power of two. The integer exponent
comes from integer register `rs1`, and the result is stored in `md`.
The type of the matrix elements is determined by `Md[ms2]`. `X[rs1]` is
zero-extended or low-bit truncated to the width of
<<ame:doc:param:AME_MAX_INT_DTYPE,AME_MAX_INT_DTYPE>> and then interpreted using
that integer datatype.  The exponent is a fixed-type control scalar and does
not read `CSR[amestype]`.
For standard floating-point data operands, a signed zero or signed infinity
preserves its sign.  The exact scaled result is rounded once on conversion to
the destination datatype.

instructions.name: mldexpacc.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise left-shift scale of `ms1` by a power of two given by `ms2`, accumulated into `md`.
`md` is both a source and destination: the existing element is read, the scaled value
is added, and the sum is written back.
For a standard tuple, `Md[ms2]` shall be an integer datatype.  An accepted
custom tuple shall define `ms2` elements as integral exponents.  The complete
expression is evaluated without an intermediate conversion to `Md[md]` and is
converted to `Md[md]` once.

instructions.name: mldexpacc.ew.x
instructions.description:
Scales every element of square `ms2` by a power of two using the integer exponent
from integer register `rs1`, then accumulates the scaled result into `md`.
`md` is both a source and destination: the existing element is read, the scaled value
is added, and the sum is written back.
The type of the matrix elements is determined by `Md[ms2]`. `X[rs1]` is
zero-extended or low-bit truncated to the width of
<<ame:doc:param:AME_MAX_INT_DTYPE,AME_MAX_INT_DTYPE>> and then interpreted using
that integer datatype.  The exponent is a fixed-type control scalar and does
not read `CSR[amestype]`.
The complete expression is evaluated without an intermediate conversion to
`Md[md]` and is converted to `Md[md]` once.

instructions.name: mlog2.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise base-2 logarithm of the tensor in `ms1`, stored into `md`.
For a standard floating-point operand, a negative finite input or `-infinity` is
invalid; `log2(±0)` is `-infinity`, `log2(+infinity)` is `+infinity`, and
`log2(1)` is `+0`.  The result is an implementation-defined approximation; the
implementation shall document the maximum error in ulp for each supported
operation/datatype tuple.

instructions.name: mlog2sub.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise biased base-2 logarithm: subtracts `ms2` from the base-2 logarithm
of the absolute value of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
For standard floating-point evaluation, the logarithm term follows the
special-value behavior of <<ame:doc:inst:mlog2_ew,mlog2.ew>>.  The
implementation shall document the maximum error in ulp for each supported
operation/datatype tuple and whether the compound expression uses an
intermediate rounding.

instructions.name: mlog2sub.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise base-2 logarithm of the absolute value of every element
of square `ms2`, subtracts a scalar bias from integer register `rs1`, and stores
the result in `md`.
For standard floating-point evaluation, the logarithm term follows the
special-value behavior of <<ame:doc:inst:mlog2_ew,mlog2.ew>>.  The
implementation shall document the maximum error in ulp for each supported
operation/datatype tuple and whether the compound expression uses an
intermediate rounding.

instructions.name: mls.1r
instructions.description:
Loads one physical M register from memory into `md` using the row-major
whole-register transfer defined by the common memory rules.
The element size is fixed at `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`.  The instruction does
not read `Md[md]`, so an uninitialized or unsupported programmed datatype does
not affect the transfer.  It transfers exactly one physical register; a wide
logical square requires one `mls.1r` for each register in its group.

instructions.name: mls.cm
instructions.description:
Loads the typed M-register operand beginning at `md` from memory in
column-major format.  The programmed datatype is read from `Md[md]`.

instructions.name: mls.rm
instructions.description:
Loads the typed M-register operand beginning at `md` from memory in row-major
format.  The programmed datatype is read from `Md[md]`.

instructions.name: mls.st
instructions.synopsis: Load square from strided memory format
instructions.description:
Loads the typed M-register operand beginning at `md` from a strided memory
layout.  The programmed datatype is read from `Md[md]`.  Memory is addressed as
row segments separated by the byte stride `X[rs2]`.

instructions.name: mls.tst
instructions.synopsis: Load square from transposed strided memory format
instructions.description:
Loads the typed M-register operand beginning at `md` from a transposed strided
memory layout.  The programmed datatype is read from `Md[md]`.  Memory is
addressed as column segments separated by the byte stride `X[rs2]`, transposing
each logical square during the transfer.

instructions.name: mmax.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise maximum of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.
`Md[ms1]`, `Md[ms2]`, and `Md[md]` shall be identical.  The common descriptor
shall be a standard numeric datatype or a custom datatype that defines the
ordering required by this operation; otherwise the tuple is unsupported under
<<norm:ame_op_supported_contract,the unsupported-datatype-tuple contract>>.
For standard floating-point operands other than NaN, the instruction selects an
operand exactly; a `-0`/`+0` tie selects `+0`.

instructions.name: mmax.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise maximum of a scalar constant from integer register `rs1`
and every element of square `ms2`, and stores the result in `md`.
`Md[ms2]` and `Md[md]` shall be identical.  The common tensor descriptor shall
be a standard numeric datatype or a custom datatype that defines the ordering
required by this operation; otherwise the tuple is unsupported under
<<norm:ame_op_supported_contract,the unsupported-datatype-tuple contract>>.
The scalar datatype need not match and follows
<<ame-common-scalar-operands,the common scalar-ingress rules>>.
For standard floating-point operands other than NaN, the instruction selects an
operand exactly; a `-0`/`+0` tie selects `+0`.

instructions.name: mmean.ew
instructions.description: Elementwise arithmetic mean of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.

instructions.name: mmean.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise mean of a scalar constant from integer register `rs1`
and every element of square `ms2`, and stores the result in `md`.

instructions.name: mmin.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise minimum of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.
`Md[ms1]`, `Md[ms2]`, and `Md[md]` shall be identical.  The common descriptor
shall be a standard numeric datatype or a custom datatype that defines the
ordering required by this operation; otherwise the tuple is unsupported under
<<norm:ame_op_supported_contract,the unsupported-datatype-tuple contract>>.
For standard floating-point operands other than NaN, the instruction selects an
operand exactly; a `-0`/`+0` tie selects `-0`.

instructions.name: mmin.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise minimum of a scalar constant from integer register `rs1`
and every element of square `ms2`, and stores the result in `md`.
`Md[ms2]` and `Md[md]` shall be identical.  The common tensor descriptor shall
be a standard numeric datatype or a custom datatype that defines the ordering
required by this operation; otherwise the tuple is unsupported under
<<norm:ame_op_supported_contract,the unsupported-datatype-tuple contract>>.
The scalar datatype need not match and follows
<<ame-common-scalar-operands,the common scalar-ingress rules>>.
For standard floating-point operands other than NaN, the instruction selects an
operand exactly; a `-0`/`+0` tie selects `-0`.

instructions.name: mmov.m.a
instructions.synopsis: Elementwise unconditional move from accumulator to M register
instructions.description:
Copies the source square from the accumulator operand to the M register `md`.
The element datatype of `acc` (from `Ad[acc]`) and `md` (from `Md[md]`)
must match; if they differ, `amestatus.UN` is set and `md` is left unchanged.
Let `N = sqrt(AME_NELEM)`.  For non-packed datatypes
(`pack_factor = 1`), the single accumulator `acc` holds one `N x N` square.
All `AME_NELEM` elements are copied to the M register group `md`; a wide
datatype occupies a group of consecutive M registers.
For packed datatypes
(`pack_factor = AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE / sizeof(Md[md]) > 1`), the
`pack_factor` consecutive accumulators starting at `acc` each hold one
`N x N` square, and all `pack_factor` squares are packed into the single M
register `md`.  If `pack_factor` exceeds
<<ame:doc:param:AME_NUM_ACC_REGS,AME_NUM_ACC_REGS>>, `amestatus.UN` is set and
`md` is left unchanged.  Otherwise, every derived accumulator index in

instructions.name: mmov.a.m
instructions.synopsis: Elementwise unconditional move from M register to accumulator
instructions.description:
Copies the source square from the M register operand `ms` to the accumulator
`acc`.

must match; if they differ, `amestatus.UN` is set and `acc` is left unchanged.

(`pack_factor = 1`), `ms` holds one `N x N` square; a wide datatype occupies
a group of consecutive M registers.  All `AME_NELEM` elements are copied to
the single accumulator `acc`.

register `ms` holds `pack_factor` `N x N` squares.  Each square is copied to
a consecutive accumulator starting at `acc`, so the instruction writes the
`pack_factor` accumulators `acc`, `acc+1`, ..., `acc + pack_factor - 1`.  If
`pack_factor` exceeds <<ame:doc:param:AME_NUM_ACC_REGS,AME_NUM_ACC_REGS>>,

derived index in that complete accumulator span is checked before any source
data is read or accumulator is written; an index greater than or equal to
`AME_NUM_ACC_REGS` raises an `Illegal Instruction` exception, and a failing
check cannot cause a partial transfer.
The operand datatypes are taken only from the base registers `Md[ms]` and
`Ad[acc]`.  As with any register group, the `Md` and `Ad` values of the
remaining registers in either group are ignored, and this instruction does
not modify any `Md` or `Ad` register.

instructions.description:

single M register `md`.  The contents of `md` are viewed, in row-major order, as

8-bit elements each, independent of the configured datatype `Md[md]`.

bits of `X[rs1]`; higher bits are ignored.  The selected column is
`pos % row_elements` and the selected row is `pos / row_elements`.
The element size is defined by
the instruction itself: it does not read `CSR[amestype]`, does not
read or convert using `Md[md]`, does not form a register group, and never
sets `amestatus.UN`.  The register contents are first normalized with the
row-major layout transformation, using the unsigned integer datatype of
size `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`, for which exactly one square occupies one M
register; the normalized image is then reinterpreted, by bit slicing, as
`N` rows of `row_elements` elements of the instruction's element size.

layout, so the position-to-element mapping is identical on every
implementation.  If one row of the row-major
view is narrower than the element size, an `Illegal Instruction` exception
is raised.

instructions.name: mmul.ew
instructions.description: Elementwise multiplication of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.

instructions.name: mmul.ew.x
instructions.description:
Multiplies every element of square `ms2` by a scalar constant from integer
register `rs1` and stores the result in `md`.

instructions.name: mmulacc.2d
instructions.description:
Accumulates the matrix product of `ms1` and `ms2` into `acc`.
`acc` is both a source and destination: its current value is read, the matrix
product is added, and the result is written back.

instructions.name: mmulacc.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise multiply-accumulate: multiplies `ms1` by `ms2` elementwise and accumulates
into `md`.
`md` is both a source and destination: the existing element is read, the product
is added, and the sum is written back.
The complete expression is evaluated without an intermediate conversion to
`Md[md]` and is converted to `Md[md]` once.  For a standard floating-point
tuple, this is a fused multiply-add with a single destination rounding.

instructions.name: mmulacc.ew.x
instructions.description:
Multiplies every element of square `ms2` by a scalar constant from integer register
`rs1` and accumulates the product into `md`.
`md` is both a source and destination: the existing element is read, the scaled product
is added, and the sum is written back.
The complete expression is evaluated without an intermediate conversion to
`Md[md]` and is converted to `Md[md]` once.  For a standard floating-point
tuple, this is a fused multiply-add with a single destination rounding.

instructions.name: mmulaccneg.2d
instructions.description:
Subtracts the matrix product of `ms1` and `ms2` from `acc`.
`acc` is both a source and destination: its current value is read, the matrix
product is subtracted, and the result is written back.

instructions.name: mmulaccneg.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise negative multiply-accumulate: multiplies `ms1` by `ms2` elementwise,
subtracts the product from `md`, and stores the result back into `md`.
`md` is both a source and destination: the existing element is read, the product
is subtracted, and the result is written back.
The complete expression is evaluated without an intermediate conversion to
`Md[md]` and is converted to `Md[md]` once.  For a standard floating-point
tuple, this is a fused multiply-subtract with a single destination rounding.

instructions.name: mmulaccneg.ew.x
instructions.description:
Multiplies every element of square `ms2` by a scalar constant from integer register
`rs1`, subtracts the product from `md`, and stores the result back into `md`.
`md` is both a source and destination: the existing element is read, the scaled product
is subtracted, and the result is written back.
The complete expression is evaluated without an intermediate conversion to
`Md[md]` and is converted to `Md[md]` once.  For a standard floating-point
tuple, this is a fused multiply-subtract with a single destination rounding.

instructions.name: mmuladd.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise fused multiply-add where `md` serves as both the multiplicand and the
destination.
`md` is both a source and destination: each existing element is multiplied by the
corresponding element of `ms2`, `ms1` is added, and the result is written back.
The complete expression is evaluated without an intermediate conversion to
`Md[md]` and is converted to `Md[md]` once.  For a standard floating-point
tuple, this is a fused multiply-add with a single destination rounding.

instructions.name: mmuladd.ew.x
instructions.description:
Elementwise scalar fused multiply-add where `md` serves as both the multiplicand and the
destination.
`md` is both a source and destination: each existing element is multiplied by the
corresponding element of `ms2`, the scalar `rs1` is added, and the result is written back.
The complete expression is evaluated without an intermediate conversion to
`Md[md]` and is converted to `Md[md]` once.  For a standard floating-point
tuple, this is a fused multiply-add with a single destination rounding.

instructions.name: mmulatacc.2d
instructions.synopsis: Matrix multiply with transposed A, accumulate
instructions.description:
Accumulates the matrix product of the transpose of `ms1` with `ms2` into `acc`.
`acc` is both a source and destination: its current value is read, the transposed-A
matrix product is added, and the result is written back.
instructions.operation: C = C + sum(transpose(A[s]) × B[s], s = 0 .. N_sq-1)

instructions.synopsis: Matrix multiply with transposed A, negated accumulate
instructions.description:

`acc` is both a source and destination: its current value is read, the transposed-A
matrix product is subtracted, and the result is written back.
instructions.operation: C = C - sum(transpose(A[s]) × B[s], s = 0 .. N_sq-1)

instructions.synopsis: Matrix multiply with transposed B, accumulate

instructions.synopsis: Matrix multiply with transposed B, negated accumulate
instructions.description:

instructions.operation: C = C - sum(A[s] × transpose(B[s]), s = 0 .. N_sq-1)

instructions.description:

instructions.description:

accepted custom tuple shall define its operand widths, raw-bit operation, and
destination representation.

instructions.description:

For standard datatypes, `Md[ms2]` and `Md[md]` shall be the same integer
datatype, and the converted scalar and matrix elements are operated on as raw
bits.  An accepted custom tuple shall define its operand widths, raw-bit
operation, and destination representation.

instructions.description:

For standard datatypes, `Md[ms1]`, `Md[ms2]`, and `Md[md]` shall be the same
integer datatype, and the operation applies to the raw element bits.  An
accepted custom tuple shall define its operand widths, raw-bit operation, and
destination representation.

instructions.description:

`rs1` with the bitwise complement of every element of square `ms2` and stores

For standard datatypes, `Md[ms2]` and `Md[md]` shall be the same integer

instructions.name: mpack.ew.x
instructions.synopsis: Pack one square into a slot of a packed M register
instructions.description:
Inserts the single non-packed square group beginning at `ms2` into the sub-square slot selected by the
index in integer register `rs1` of the packed M register `md`, converting each element
from the non-packed datatype (`Md[ms2]`) to the packed datatype (`Md[md]`). The other
sub-square slots of `md` are preserved (read-modify-write).
`Md[md]` must be a packed datatype and `Md[ms2]` a non-packed datatype; otherwise
`amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written. For
`pack_factor = AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE / sizeof(Md[md])`, the index is the low
`log2(pack_factor)` bits of `X[rs1]`; higher X-register bits are ignored.  The
index is a fixed-type unsigned control scalar and does not read
`CSR[amestype]`.

instructions.name: mprefixadd.col
instructions.description:
Computes an inclusive prefix sum (running sum) along each column of `ms1` and
stores the result in `md`.
Let `A_D[i,j]` denote `ms1[i,j]` converted to `Md[md]`.
The accepted exact tuple shall define the source-to-destination conversion and
addition of two `Md[md]` values; otherwise the tuple is unsupported under
<<norm:ame_op_supported_contract,the unsupported-datatype-tuple contract>>.
Each source conversion applies the destination conversion's rounding,
saturation, and accrued status-flag behavior before the converted value
participates in the fold.  No semantic-zero term is introduced.
For a standard floating-point destination, each output `D[i,j]` uses an
implementation-defined association tree whose leaves are exactly
`A_D[k,j]` for `k = 0 .. i`.  Every tree node adds two `Md[md]` values, rounds
the result to `Md[md]`, and accrues the applicable status flags.  For every
other accepted destination, the first converted element initializes the
running result and the remaining converted elements are consumed in ascending
row-index order.  Each destination-domain addition applies the destination
rounding, saturation, and accrued status-flag behavior before its result is
used by the next step.

instructions.name: mprefixadd.row
instructions.description:
Computes an inclusive prefix sum (running sum) along each row of `ms1` and
stores the result in `md`.
Let `A_D[i,j]` denote `ms1[i,j]` converted to `Md[md]`.
The accepted exact tuple shall define the source-to-destination conversion and
addition of two `Md[md]` values; otherwise the tuple is unsupported under
<<norm:ame_op_supported_contract,the unsupported-datatype-tuple contract>>.
Each source conversion applies the destination conversion's rounding,
saturation, and accrued status-flag behavior before the converted value
participates in the fold.  No semantic-zero term is introduced.
For a standard floating-point destination, each output `D[i,j]` uses an
implementation-defined association tree whose leaves are exactly
`A_D[i,k]` for `k = 0 .. j`.  Every tree node adds two `Md[md]` values, rounds
the result to `Md[md]`, and accrues the applicable status flags.  For every
other accepted destination, the first converted element initializes the
running result and the remaining converted elements are consumed in ascending
column-index order.  Each destination-domain addition applies the destination
rounding, saturation, and accrued status-flag behavior before its result is
used by the next step.

instructions.name: mprefixmax.col
instructions.description:
Computes a running maximum (inclusive prefix max) along each column of `ms1`
and stores the result in `md`.
Let `A_D[i,j]` denote `ms1[i,j]` converted to `Md[md]`.
The accepted exact tuple shall define the source-to-destination conversion and

`CSR[amestype]`, and is reduced modulo the `ms2` element width.  An accepted
custom tuple shall define its logical-shift behavior and result representation.

instructions.name: mss.1r
instructions.description:
Stores one physical M register `ms1` to memory using the row-major
whole-register transfer defined by the common memory rules.
The element size is fixed at `AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE`.  The instruction does
not read `Md[ms1]`, so an uninitialized or unsupported programmed datatype does
not affect the transfer.  It transfers exactly one physical register; a wide
logical square requires one `mss.1r` for each register in its group.

instructions.name: mss.cm
instructions.description:
Stores the typed M-register operand beginning at `ms1` to memory in
column-major format.  The programmed datatype is read from `Md[ms1]`.

instructions.name: mss.rm
instructions.description:
Stores the typed M-register operand beginning at `ms1` to memory in row-major
format.  The programmed datatype is read from `Md[ms1]`.

instructions.name: mss.st
instructions.synopsis: Store square to strided memory format
instructions.description:
Stores the typed M-register operand beginning at `ms1` to a strided memory
layout.  The programmed datatype is read from `Md[ms1]`.  Memory is addressed as
row segments separated by the byte stride `X[rs2]`.

instructions.name: mss.tst
instructions.synopsis: Store square to transposed strided memory format
instructions.description:
Stores the typed M-register operand beginning at `ms1` to a transposed strided
memory layout.  The programmed datatype is read from `Md[ms1]`.  Memory is
addressed as column segments separated by the byte stride `X[rs2]`, transposing
each logical square during the transfer.

instructions.name: msub.ew
instructions.description: Subtracts `ms1` from `ms2` elementwise and stores the result in `md`.

instructions.name: msub.ew.x
instructions.description:
Subtracts the scalar in integer register `rs1` from every element of `ms2`
and stores the result in `md`.

instructions.name: msublog2.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise complementary biased base-2 logarithm: subtracts the base-2 logarithm
of the absolute value of `ms1` from `ms2`, stored into `md`.
For standard floating-point evaluation, the logarithm term follows the
special-value behavior of <<ame:doc:inst:mlog2_ew,mlog2.ew>>.  The
implementation shall document the maximum error in ulp for each supported
operation/datatype tuple and whether the compound expression uses an
intermediate rounding.

instructions.name: msublog2.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise base-2 logarithm of the absolute value of every element
of square `ms2`, subtracts each result from a scalar constant from integer
register `rs1`, and stores the result in `md`.
For standard floating-point evaluation, the logarithm term follows the
special-value behavior of <<ame:doc:inst:mlog2_ew,mlog2.ew>>.  The
implementation shall document the maximum error in ulp for each supported
operation/datatype tuple and whether the compound expression uses an
intermediate rounding.

instructions.name: mtanh.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise hyperbolic tangent of `ms1`, stored into `md`.
For a standard floating-point operand, `tanh(±0)` preserves its zero sign and
`tanh(±infinity)` is `±1`.  The result is an implementation-defined
approximation; the implementation shall document the maximum error in ulp for
each supported operation/datatype tuple.

instructions.name: munpack.ew.x
instructions.synopsis: Unpack one sub-square from a packed M register
instructions.description:
Extracts a single sub-square, selected by the index in integer register `rs1`, from the
packed M register `ms2` and writes it to the non-packed M register group beginning at `md`, converting each
element from the packed datatype (`Md[ms2]`) to the non-packed datatype (`Md[md]`).
`Md[ms2]` must be a packed datatype and `Md[md]` a non-packed datatype; otherwise
`amestatus.UN` is set and no register is written. For
`pack_factor = AME_UNIT_DATATYPE_SIZE / sizeof(Md[ms2])`, the index is the low
`log2(pack_factor)` bits of `X[rs1]`; higher X-register bits are ignored.  The
index is a fixed-type unsigned control scalar and does not read
`CSR[amestype]`.

instructions.name: mxor.ew
instructions.description:
Elementwise bitwise XOR of the tensors in `ms1` and `ms2`, stored into `md`.
For standard datatypes, `Md[ms1]`, `Md[ms2]`, and `Md[md]` shall be the same
integer datatype, and the operation applies to the raw element bits.  An
accepted custom tuple shall define its operand widths, raw-bit operation, and
destination representation.

instructions.name: mxor.ew.x
instructions.description:
Computes the elementwise bitwise XOR of a scalar constant from integer register
`rs1` with every element of square `ms2` and stores the result in `md`.
For standard datatypes, `Md[ms2]` and `Md[md]` shall be the same integer
datatype, and the converted scalar and matrix elements are operated on as raw
bits.  An accepted custom tuple shall define its operand widths, raw-bit
operation, and destination representation.

instructions.name: mzero.2d.acc
instructions.description: Writes zero to every element of `acc`.

instructions.name: mzero.2d.m
instructions.description: Writes zero to every element of the M register group `md`.
